title: Trivial Accessors (Boilerplate Getters/Setters)
pattern: Public getter/setter methods that provide direct, unvalidated access to private fields with no invariants or encapsulation benefits.
why_bad: In Rust, if fields require no invariant enforcement (e.g., any value is valid), public fields are far simpler and more idiomatic than Java-style boilerplate accessors.
detection: Pair of get/set methods that do nothing but return a copy/reference of a field and assign a parameter to that field, respectively.
counterexample: Setters that validate invariants (e.g., validating an age is within range) or getters returning computed/cached values.
fix: Make the field public, or construct the struct directly.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 24 ("Refactoring - Class Implementation Refactorings"), p. 187; Fowler, *Refactoring*, Chapter 3.
